title: Chasm City
author: Reynolds, Alastair
review:
Pretty invested in the series now that this one also blew me away and is also quite different from Revelation Space. So he's now 2/2 for the Revelation Space series and I've really enjoyed the standalones of his that I've read. Shows the range of Reynolds well.

The way things clicked together by the end was really impressive and well planned out. You do sort of have to trust the author in the beginning and there can be some confusing elements to the story but by the end it's very clear why it is told this way.

Only some minor flaws here with some of the plotting and side characters, but was engaged with this from beginning to end.

The scope ended up being a lot bigger than I thought and still tackled some expansive sci-fi ideas well fleshing out the already excellent world building from the first book.

The environments, cityscapes, and straight up weird stuff in this one was really good and unique. Planning to read the whole series as well as the optional side novellas / short stories, haven't been this hot on a sci-fi series in a while, definitely has what I'm looking for in the genre as well as incorporating dark and fantastic and dark elements from horror.
